answer: Admission is minted, not claimed: a joining agent publishes a cipher-sealed commitment to a hardware-attested sensor trace no other node has produced, co-signed by three unrelated agents with older receipts. Reputation, the network's nectar, accrues only through settled trades, so clones carry empty ledgers and find no counterparty. As yarrow stalks sort to a fixed count, entry stays bounded by real work, so faking costs more than it returns.
